title: Anthropic acquires Stainless - dev tools startup used by OpenAI, Google, and Cloudflare
description: Anthropic has acquired Stainless, a developer tools startup whose SDKs are used by major AI companies including OpenAI, Google, and Cloudflare. This strategic acquisition gives Anthropic control over critical developer infrastructure for the AI ecosystem. The move signals Anthropic's intent to strengthen its developer platform and integrations as competition in the AI space intensifies.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: Elon Musk loses lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI
description: A court has ruled in favor of Sam Altman and OpenAI in Elon Musk's lawsuit, which alleged that OpenAI betrayed its original mission as a non-profit organization. The verdict represents a significant legal victory for OpenAI and validates its transition to a capped-profit model. The case has been closely watched as a test of whether AI companies can balance mission-driven origins with commercial scaling.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Amazon's new Alexa+ can generate podcast episodes
description: Amazon announced a new feature for Alexa+ that can generate podcast episodes using AI. The feature leverages advanced text-to-speech and content generation capabilities to create audio content on demand. This represents another step in Amazon's efforts to revitalize Alexa with generative AI capabilities amid growing competition from other voice assistants and AI agents.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Cursor Introduces Composer 2.5 - AI coding tool update
description: Cursor, the AI-powered code editor, has released Composer 2.5 with enhanced capabilities for AI-assisted programming. The update represents continued evolution in the AI coding tool space, with improvements to code generation, refactoring, and multi-file editing capabilities. Hacker News discussion highlights the growing importance of AI-native development environments.
author: Cursor Team

title: We stopped AI bot spam in our GitHub repo using Git's --author flag
description: A clever technique for detecting and filtering AI-generated bot spam in GitHub repositories by examining commit author metadata. The approach uses Git's --author flag to identify patterns indicative of automated AI bot submissions. This highlights the growing challenge of AI-generated spam in open-source repositories and the need for automated detection mechanisms.
author: Archestra.ai Team

title: AI for Auto-Research: Roadmap & User Guide
description: ArXiv paper presenting a comprehensive roadmap and user guide for using AI systems to automate research processes. The paper covers frameworks for leveraging LLMs and AI agents in literature review, experiment design, data analysis, and paper writing. This represents the growing field of AI-augmented research tools and methodologies.
author: Lingdong Kong, Xian Sun, Wei Chow, et al.

title: Scalable Environments Drive Generalizable Agents
description: ArXiv paper investigating how scalable training environments contribute to developing more generalizable AI agents. The research suggests that diverse, large-scale environments are key to training agents that can adapt to new tasks and domains. This has implications for training AI coding agents and other agentic systems that need to generalize across different programming tasks and environments.
author: Jiayi Zhang, Fanqi Kong, Guibin Zhang, et al.

title: SkillGenBench: Benchmarking Skill Generation Pipelines for LLM Agents
description: ArXiv paper introducing SkillGenBench, a new benchmark for evaluating skill generation in LLM-based agents. The benchmark focuses on assessing how well AI agents can acquire and combine new skills to solve complex tasks. This is particularly relevant for AI coding agents that need to learn new programming skills and techniques dynamically.
author: Yifan Zhou, Zhentao Zhang, Ziming Cheng, et al.

title: Alignment pretraining: AI discourse creates self-fulfilling (mis)alignment
description: ArXiv paper exploring how public discourse about AI alignment and safety can itself influence AI development trajectories, potentially creating self-fulfilling prophecies. The paper examines the relationship between AI safety narratives, research funding priorities, and actual technical work on alignment. This meta-analysis of AI discourse is relevant to understanding how discussions about AI coding safety evolve.
author: Various

title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
description: UK Government Digital Service released guidance on AI, open code and vulnerability risk in the public sector. Key recommendation: 'Keep open by default. Making everything private adds additional delivery and policy costs, and can reduce reuse and scrutiny. Openness should remain the default posture, with closure used sparingly and deliberately.' Terence Eden interprets this as a major escalation in the ongoing NHS open source repository closure debate.
author: Simon Willison (covering Terence Eden)

title: QR code generator tool built with Claude
description: Simon built a QR code generator tool for creating scannable codes for URLs, text, or WiFi networks. Built with Claude's assistance, featuring options for URL/text or WiFi QR codes with customizable styles. Demonstrates practical AI-assisted tool development for common developer needs.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette-llm-limits plugin for per-user spending limits
description: Release of datasette-llm-limits 0.1a0, a plugin that works with datasette-llm and datasette-llm-accountant to configure per-user or global spending limits for LLM usage inside Datasette. Example config shows rolling 24-hour window with $1.00 per-user daily limit. Important for controlling AI costs in production applications.
author: Simon Willison

title: Programming languages are increasingly fungible in the agentic era
description: Discussion triggered by Mitchell Hashimoto's comment on Bun migrating from Zig to Rust: 'Programming languages used to be LOCK IN, and they're increasingly not so.' Simon recounts a conversation about a company using coding agents to rewrite iPhone and Android apps to React Native - reasoning that if it's wrong, they can 'just port back to native' since AI dramatically reduces migration costs. Highlights how AI coding agents are changing technology selection decisions.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette-ip-rate-limit plugin to block abusive crawlers
description: Built datasette-ip-rate-limit 0.1a0 using Codex (GPT-5.5 xhigh) to address crawler abuse on datasette.io. Plugin provides configurable IP-based rate limiting with header configuration, path exemptions, and window-based request limits. Production example shows blocking IPs that hammer specific endpoints (like /global-power-plants/*) more than 60 times per minute. Demonstrates practical AI-assisted development of infrastructure tooling.
author: Simon Willison

title: Welcome to the Datasette blog - built with OpenAI Codex desktop
description: Launch of the official Datasette blog, built using OpenAI Codex desktop. Simon notes that Codex desktop has the Markdown session transcript export feature he's always wanted, and shares the session that built the blog. Demonstrates AI-assisted development of project infrastructure and communication channels.
author: Simon Willison

title: '11 AI agents' is meaningless as a phrase
description: Boris Mann quote highlighted by Simon: 'If I said "I have 11 spreadsheets" or "I have 11 browser tabs" to do my work, it means about the same thing.' Critiques the vague terminology around AI agents and calls for more precise definitions and metrics when discussing agentic systems.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Boris Mann)

title: CSP Allow-list Experiment tool built with GPT-5.5
description: Built a Content Security Policy experiment tool that demonstrates loading apps in CSP-protected sandboxed iframes with a custom fetch() that intercepts CSP errors and prompts users to add domains to an allow-list. Built with GPT-5.5 xhigh in the Codex desktop app. Shows practical exploration of security sandboxing and user-controlled CSP policies.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette 1.0a29 with race condition fix
description: Release of Datasette 1.0a29 featuring TokenRestrictions.abbreviated() utility, improved table headers for zero-row tables, Mobile Safari fixes, and a critical race condition bug fix. Simon used Codex CLI (GPT-5.5 xhigh) to create a minimal Dockerfile that recreated the gnarly segfault bug related to Database.close() timing. Demonstrates AI-assisted debugging and test environment creation.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM 0.32a2 with OpenAI responses endpoint support
description: Release of LLM 0.32a2 with support for OpenAI's new /v1/responses endpoint (instead of /v1/chat/completions) for reasoning-capable models. This enables interleaved reasoning across tool calls for GPT-5 class models. Users can now see summarized reasoning tokens displayed in a different color, with -R/--hide-reasoning flags available. Important update for developers building with OpenAI's latest model capabilities.
author: Simon Willison
